title: Augustus Expels Astrologers and Magicians from Rome
description: Augustus expelled astrologers and magicians from the city of Rome in 33 BCE, establishing a pattern of imperial regulation of divination and magical practice that would characterize the early empire. The expulsion reflected anxiety about political uses of prophecy and astrology in a period of political instability, as such practitioners could spread destabilizing predictions about rulers' fates. This represents the first of several such expulsions under different emperors and illustrates the Roman state's concern with magical practice primarily as a political threat. Subsequent emperors including Tiberius and Domitian would conduct similar expulsions.
historiographical_note: Tamsyn Barton's work on ancient astrology and Frederick Cramer's study of astrology in Roman law both analyze these periodic expulsions as evidence of political rather than purely religious motivations for Roman magic regulation.
source_method: Published scholarship; Cassius Dio 49.43; Suetonius Augustus 31
